summary: Polygon's guide to the Warlock class in Baldur's Gate 3, covering class features, cantrips, spells, proficiencies, and the three subclasses. It explains that Warlocks use Charisma, have few but powerful spell slots that recharge on a short rest, and recommends Great Old One as the most broadly useful subclass. It also suggests racial weapon and armor proficiencies, stat priorities, and feats like Actor, Elemental Adept, Moderately Armored, and Spell Sniper.
one_line: A guide to the Warlock class in Baldur's Gate 3, including subclasses, stat priorities, recommended feats, and build advice.
key_facts: The Warlock is one of twelve classes in Baldur's Gate 3, and its primary ability score is Charisma.
Every Warlock spell slot is the highest level available, and Warlock spell slots recharge on a short rest instead of a long rest.
Warlocks have 1d8 Hit Dice per level and 8 + Constitution modifier hit points at 1st level, then 5 + Constitution modifier per level after 1st.
Warlocks start with two cantrips and two spells, and two of the spells are exclusive to the chosen subclass.
Warlock proficiencies are Simple Weapons, Light Armor, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws, and two skills chosen from Arcana, Deception, History, Intimidation, Investigation, Nature, and Religion.
The three Warlock subclasses are The Fiend, The Great Old One, and The Archfey, and all are available from the start of the game.
The Fiend subclass gets 'Dark One's Blessing' (four temporary hit points when defeating a hostile creature) and the spells Burning Hands and Command.
The Great Old One gets 'Mortal Reminder' (frightens a creature and nearby enemies after a critical hit unless they pass a Wisdom save) and the spells Dissonant Whispers and Tasha's Hideous Laughter.
The Archfey gets the 'Fey Presence' action (charm or frighten nearby foes) and the spells Faerie Fire and Sleep.
Charisma should be the highest stat and Constitution the second highest, since Warlocks tend to be glass cannons like Sorcerers.

The Eldritch Invocation gained at level 2, which turns Eldritch Blast into an Agonizing Blast, matters more than the pact chosen at level 1, but Great Old One is recommended for the most broadly useful features.
Helpful racial proficiencies include Drow Weapon Training, Civil Militia for Humans and Half-Elves, Githyanki Martial Prodigy, and Dwarven Combat Training (Shield Dwarf also gets Medium Armor).
Recommended feats are Actor, Elemental Adept, Moderately Armored, and Spell Sniper, with a stat increase or feat available every four levels.
